deepDive.title: NPK chemistry — what's actually in your bag of fertiliser
deepDive.body: Class 7 shows soil supports plants. Class 8 names the three macronutrients plants need most: NITROGEN (N), PHOSPHORUS (P), POTASSIUM (K). Every fertiliser bag in India shows three numbers like 20-20-0 — that's % N, % P, % K. Urea (most popular Indian fertiliser): 46-0-0, pure nitrogen. DAP (diammonium phosphate): 18-46-0, balanced N+P. MOP (potassium chloride): 0-0-60, pure potassium. Why three numbers? Nitrogen makes leaves green and lush. Phosphorus drives roots and flowers. Potassium builds disease resistance and water regulation. Different crops need different ratios — paddy needs more N, mangoes more K. Soil testing by Krishi Vigyan Kendras tells farmers which combination to use. Without this chemistry knowledge, fertilizers either under-feed (poor yield) or over-feed (water pollution).
deepDive.nextStepHint: Class 11 covers micronutrients (iron, zinc, manganese) — needed in tiny amounts but equally critical.

deepDive.title: Erosion processes — water, wind, and the loss of Indian topsoil
deepDive.body: Class 7 says erosion strips soil. Class 10 names the processes. SHEET EROSION: thin layer of topsoil swept off by surface runoff. GULLY EROSION: deep channels cut by concentrated water flow. RILL EROSION: small channels, in between. WIND EROSION: dry, bare topsoil blown away by strong winds (worst in Rajasthan). Indian numbers are alarming: ~5300 million tonnes of topsoil lost annually. The Chambal ravines (MP) are textbook gully-eroded landscape — formed in decades from clearing forests. Solutions: terracing (cuts slope), contour ploughing (perpendicular to slope), cover crops (no bare soil), shelterbelts (trees blocking wind). Each works at a specific scale — terracing is village-level engineering; cover crops are individual-farm decisions.
deepDive.prerequisite: Tackle after Class 7 soil erosion basics.
deepDive.nextStepHint: JEE / Civil engineering students study soil mechanics — quantitative models of erosion rates.

deepDive.title: Pedogenesis — how soil ITSELF forms from rock
deepDive.body: Class 7 says soil is bits of rock + organic matter. Class 11 names the formation process: PEDOGENESIS — soil genesis. Five factors (CLORPT acronym): Climate (temperature, rainfall drive weathering rates); Organisms (lichens, then bacteria, then plants colonise rock); Relief (slope shapes soil depth); Parent material (the rock determines the chemistry); Time (millennia to form). A 30 cm soil profile typically takes 1000-10,000 years. The famous Indian black cotton soil (Deccan) formed from basalt + millennia of weathering — it's why Maharashtra grows cotton so well. Once eroded, you can't 'just regrow' soil — it's a geological-time resource. This is why every farmer protecting his soil today is gifting the next 5 generations.
deepDive.prerequisite: Tackle after Class 7 soil profile basics.
deepDive.nextStepHint: Class 12 environmental science quantifies soil loss in tonnes per hectare per year.
